chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-ʿAbdī, from Ḥamzah ibn Ḥumrān, from Ḥumrān, who said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام. I said to him: When does it become obligatory that the full legal penalties be applied to the boy, established upon him, and that he be held to them?

He said: “When orphanhood has passed from him and he has reached maturity.” I said: Is there a known limit for that? He said: “When he experiences a wet dream, or reaches fifteen years, or grows hair, or sprouts before that, then the full legal penalties are established upon him, he is held to them, and they are also taken for him.”

I said: Then when does the girl become subject to the full legal penalties, is held to them, and they are taken for her? He said: “Indeed, the girl is not like the boy. Indeed, when the girl marries, and the marriage is consummated with her, and she is nine years old, orphanhood has passed from her, her property is handed over to her, her authority in purchase and sale becomes valid, and the full legal penalties are established upon her, and they are taken for her and against her.”

He said: “And the boy’s authority in purchase and sale is not valid, and he does not leave orphanhood until he reaches fifteen years, or experiences a wet dream, or grows hair, or sprouts before that.”

key_terms.احْتَلَمَ: experienced a wet dream, indicating biological maturity
key_terms.الشِّرَاءِ وَالْبَيْعِ: buying and selling; legal capacity in financial transactions
key_terms.الْحُدُودِ التَّامَّةِ: the full prescribed legal penalties and liabilities in Islamic law
key_terms.الْيُتْمُ: orphanhood; the legal state of being a minor whose father has died
key_terms.تِسْعُ سِنِينَ: nine years of age, mentioned here regarding the girl
key_terms.خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً: fifteen years of age, a legal marker of maturity for the boy in this report
key_terms.دُخِلَ بِهَا: the marriage was consummated with her

ai.seo_question: When do full legal responsibilities and hudud apply to a boy or girl in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal markers for the end of minority and the beginning of full legal responsibility in the case of boys and girls. It addresses the application of hudud, the end of orphan status, and the validity of financial dealings, distinguishing between the legal signs relevant to each.
